requirement:
YAML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment,
including a comment following a mapping value. A `#` within quoted text or
within the content of a block scalar belongs to the scalar.
rationale:
The `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.attachments` requirement is adequately tested by the `test.yaml` case in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. That test carries a `{test}` reference to the requirement.

The source is `a: |\n  # literal\n# standalone\nb: '# literal' # real\nc: "# literal"\n`. The test collects every attachment from the outline items. It asserts with `assert_eq!` that the exact list is `[(Comment, "# standalone"), (Comment, "# real")]`.

Mapping of obligations to the test:
- **Only `Comment` attachments.** The expected list contains only `Comment` kinds. Any `Annotation` or other kind would fail the equality check.
- **Each `#` comment is one attachment.** The standalone comment and the trailing comment each produce exactly one attachment with the right span. The test compares the whole list, so an extra, missing or merged attachment would fail.
- **A comment following a mapping value.** `b: '# literal' # real` yields `# real` as a separate attachment.
- **A `#` inside a block scalar belongs to the scalar.** The `# literal` line under `a: |` is not reported.
- **A `#` inside quoted text belongs to the scalar.** The single-quoted `'# literal'` and the double-quoted `"# literal"` are not reported.

One scenario is not covered: two adjacent standalone comment lines in YAML. The text does not call out that case. The same test checks it for TOML (`# first`, `# second`), and the YAML provider uses the same tree-sitter comment handling, so I do not count it as a gap. The test asserts every scenario the text names, so I found no adequacy gap.
